An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map and Rezoning Certain Lands Known As Eagle Mountain Retail.
items.background: (Presented by Senior Planner David Stroud) The proposed ordinance amends the General Plan Land Use Map from Neighborhood Residential One and Community Commercial to Regional Commercial and Parks and Open Space, and rezones the subject parcel from Agriculture and Commercial to Commercial Regional and Open Space-I for the purpose of permitting "big box" development. The subject property is located at the northwest intersection of SR-73 and Spring Run Parkway. This is the proposed location for a Walmart Supercenter.

items.title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Eagle Mountain Retail Development Agreement with Armstrong Commercial Services.
items.background: (Presented by Senior Planner David Stroud) The proposed development agreement is in relation to a large-scale retail development on Parcel 58:033:0404.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Amendment to the General Plan Future Land Use Map from Agriculture/Rural Density 1 to Agriculture/Rural Density 2, and Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Eagle Mountain Benches from RA2 and AG to RD1.
items.background: (Presented by Planning Manager Robert Hobbs) The proposed ordinance amends the Eagle Mountain City General Plan Future Land Use Map and rezones approximately 102 acres of property on Utah County Parcel Numbers 59:006:0042, 59:006:0046, 59:006:0047, 59:006:0054, and 59:006:0055. The applications also include a request to waive the Master Development requirements found in EMMC 16.10 Master Developments. This item was remanded back to the Planning Commission at the May 16, 2023 City Council meeting to consider all of the applicants’ land and provide a recommendation regarding the minimum average lot size.

items.title: Request for the Waiver of the Master Development Approval Requirement for Eagle Mountain Benches.
items.background: (Presented by Planning Manager Robert Hobbs) The applicants are requesting the City Council waive the requirements found in Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.10 Master Developments.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.75 Standards for Special Uses, and Sections 17.20.050 Conditional Uses (Agriculture Zone), 17.35.030 Land Use Table (Commercial Zones), and 17.40.040 Conditional Uses (Industrial Zone) Regarding Automobile Sales, Kennels, Racetracks, and Communication Facility Generators.
items.background: (Presented by Planner Steven Lehmitz) The proposed ordinance adds kennels as a Conditional Use in the Agriculture and Industrial Zones, adds racetracks as a Conditional Use in the Industrial Zone, outlines Special Use standards for automobile sales and racetrack uses, and permits generators in conjunction with communication facilities and towers. The amendment also removes superscript "5" from the Commercial Zone Land Use Table; the footnote stating, "These special uses are considered prohibited until special use standards specific to these uses are approved and included in Chapter 17.75 EMMC." This item was tabled at the June 20, 2023 City Council meeting, and the public hearing was continued to this meeting.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10 Definitions, Chapter 17.38 Commercial Storage Zone, and Chapter 17.40 Industrial Zone, Regarding Caretaker Dwellings.
items.background: (Presented by Senior Planner David Stroud) The proposed ordinance amends EMMC Chapter 17.10 Definitions to add "Caretaker Dwelling," and amends Chapter 17.38 Commercial Storage Zone and Chapter 17.40 Industrial Zone to permit a caretaker dwelling as a conditional use in each zone. This item was tabled at the June 20, 2023 City Council meeting, and the public hearing was continued to this meeting. ORD--EMMC Title 17 Changes - Caretaker Dwellings EMMC 17.10, 17.38, & 17.40 Caretaker Dwellings - Redlines

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.10 Definitions, 17.25 Residential Zones, 17.72 Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards, and 17.55 Off-street Parking Regarding Alleys and Service Drives, Fire Department-related Access Standards, and ADA Parking Standards.
items.background: (Presented by Planning Manager Robert Hobbs) The proposed ordinance includes amendments to Title 17 that provide definitions and parameters for alleys, service drives and ADA parking clarifications. This item was tabled at the June 20, 2023, City Council meeting, and the public hearing was continued to this meeting.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.56 Vacation of Rights-of-Way.
items.background: (Presented by Planning Manager Robert Hobbs) The proposed ordinance enacts EMMC Chapter 16.56 Vacation of Rights-of-Way to allow for the vacation of public streets and alleys without having to execute a plat amendment. This item was tabled at the June 20, 2023 City Council meeting, and the public hearing was continued to this meeting.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code, Section 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, Regarding Golf Course Netting.
items.background: (Presented by Senior Planner David Stroud) The proposed ordinance amends EMMC Section 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, to create netting standards on property adjacent to a golf course.

items.title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, and Eagle Mountain City for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property Within the Sweetwater Industrial Park Community Reinvestment Area #3.
items.background: (Presented by Economic Development Director Evan Berrett) This project allows for the creation of a Community Reinvestment Area in order to allow for a data center project development on approximately 490 acres on the western border of the Meta datacenter property. When all phases have been triggered for the first six buildings, the City will receive approximately $140,000 annually in property tax until the incentive expires. The interlocal agreement allows Utah County to transmit certain incremental tax revenue for Eagle Mountain City to the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City for execution of the project area plan and budget.

items.title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the QTS Eagle Mountain I, LLC Development Agreement.
items.background: (Presented by Economic Development Director Evan Berrett) The development agreement relates to the development of the QTS Eagle Mountain I, LLC property within the Sweetwater Industrial Park Community Reinvestment Area #3.

items.title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.16.030 Hiring and Employment Terms to Remove Reference to a Six-Month Severance Stipulation.
items.background: (Presented by City Attorney Marcus Draper) The proposed ordinance amends Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.16.030 Hiring and Employment Terms to remove the stipulation that severance benefits for a city administrator shall not exceed six months.

October 13, 2020, Planning Commission Minutes

Pony Express Townhomes (Concept Plan) Concept plan review for the next phase of Pony Express Townhomes located on approximately 4.6 acres. Access to this portion of the development would be off of N Sun Crest Drive in the New Park at Porter's Crossing subdivision. The concept plan includes 27 townhome units, with nine buildings of three units each.

Scenic Mountain Phase C (Concept Plan) A concept plan for Phase C of the Scenic Mountain project. The Scenic Mountain project includes an approved Master Development Agreement (MDA). Portions of Phases A and B have been built or are under construction. The applicant is looking to develop the plans for Phase C based on the and is seeking feedback on the concept plan before submitting their next set of applications.

Oquirrh Mountain Ranch Phase B (Concept Plan) A concept plan for Phase B of the Oquirrh Mountain Ranch project. The Oquirrh Mountain Ranch project includes an approved Master Development Agreement. A majority of Phase A has been built. The applicant is considering an amendment request to the Master Development Agreement with regards to Phase B and is seeking feedback on the concept plan.

Development Code Amendment to Remove Tier and Bonus Density Language (EMMC Titles 7, 16, and 17) This is a request to amend the municipal development code for EMMC Title 7 Parks, Trails and Special Events; Title 16 Subdivisions; and Title 17 Zoning in order to remove references to "tier" and "base/bonus density." These phrases related to EMMC 17.30 Residential Zone Bonus Density Entitlements which was repealed by ordinance of the City Council in 2019.

Development Code Amendment for Fencing Standards (EMMC 16.35 & 17.60) This is a request to amend the municipal development code for EMMC Chapter 16.35 Development Standards for Required Public Facilities and Chapter 17.60 Landscaping, Buffering, Fencing and Transitioning. The amendment includes revisions to clarify fencing standards and requirements. The Planning Commission held a public hearing on this request on October 13, 2020. The public hearing was opened and closed at that time. The request was tabled for minor edits to the code amendment.

items.title: May 5, 2026 Minutes - Regular Redevelopment Agency Board Meeting

A Resolution of the Redevelopment Agency Board of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Issuance of the Agency's Sales Tax and Tax Increment Revenue Bonds, Series 2026 (the "Bonds") in Par Amount of Not to Exceed $10,000,000 and Authorizing the Execution of Related Bond Documents Thereto and all other Actions Required to Issue the Bonds.
items.background: (Presented by Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch) This resolution authorizes the City to pledge a portion of its sales and use tax revenue toward the Redevelopment Agency’s Series 2026 bonds to finance these infrastructure improvements. The project involves a proposed 50-acre retail development anchored by Smith’s Marketplace and Lowe’s Home Improvement, using CRA and TIF financing to help fund nearby roadway improvements, including Old Airport Road, Lake Mountain Corridor, and Pony Express Parkway. The City Council previously directed Staff on May 19, 2026, to move forward with financing options to support favorable bond terms.
